newsitem.title: FRANCE: RALLYING-MAKINEN HITS COW, DROPS OUT OF CORSICA RALLY.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MAKINEN HITS COW, DROPS OUT OF CORSICA RALLY.

text.p: World champion Tommi Makinen had to pull out of the Tour of Corsica rally after hitting a cow in the first of Tuesday's six timed stages, his team said.
Finn Makinen was halfway through the 48.9-km test from Vero to Liamone, the longest of this year's rally, when his Mitsubishi Lancer bumped into a cow and went off the road.
Neither Makinen nor co-driver Seppo Harjanne was hurt but the car was destroyed and they were unable to restart, a Mitsubishi spokesman said.

Makinen, who had won the last two rallies in Portugal and Spain and was leading the championship standings, had started the second day of the three-day event in sixth position, 38 seconds behind leader Gilles Panizzi of France, in a Peugeot 306.

Tuesday's gruelling first section in the mountains north of Ajaccio went to Spaniard Carlos Sainz, whose four-wheel drive Ford Escort gained 46 seconds on Panizzi's lightweight, two-wheel drive machine.

Frenchman Francois Delecour, in the other Peugeot 306, clocked the second-fastest time 10 seconds slower than Sainz to seize the overall lead. But the Spaniard, who won in Corsica in 1991, was dangerously close, just four seconds back in second place.

Armin Schwarz of Germany, who was already out of contention for final victory on Wednesday, experienced more trouble as he lost the rear left wheel of his Ford Escort and had to drive the last 17 kilometres of the stretch to Liamone on three wheels.
